label: Frontier growth must be a typed proposal the workflow converts, never a leaf write: S1 GraphPatchProposalV1 names the affected frontier and creates a new topology version; S5 makes need_new_source_scope, need_parallel_work and propose_next_focus typed data only the enclosing workflow may turn into an edge or dispatch. Runtime map: the leaf emits frontier-node proposals in its delta, and the YAML/reducer becomes the missing automated writer of research/inbox.jsonl. Design-level, not shipped.

Depth and breadth are bounded by narrow-only inheritance and nested budgets: a sealed child binds max depth, child count and a conserved budget slice and may only narrow them (S6 P5); budgets nest run>subgraph>node>attempt and exhaustion picks an explicit edge, never weakening gates (S1); admission order is registry>policy>budget>depth>reachability>acyclicity with a worst-case estimate plus a runtime meter (reference/03). Runtime map: frontier nodes carry depth and parentId; config adds maxDepth, maxFrontierNodes and a per-node iteration slice; an admission check runs before any inbox write.

The graph program's stop rule is obligation accounting, not novelty: completeness means every scoped obligation is accounted for, including blockers and negative results, and a bounded loop may end abstain, blocked or exhausted (S6). S4 and S6 both treat the falling self-reported novelty ratio as corpus-exhaustion telemetry, not convergence proof. Runtime map: expansive stop = frontier empty (each node answered|blocked|exhausted|abstained) or budget spent; newInfoRatio becomes a per-node signal.

Keep the shipped StopDecision live and add frontier logic beside it: S6 states the S5 StopDecision remains the live per-loop stop owner and a graph convergence gate is a separate target-state addition; S5 says do not replace the rolling-novelty/MAD/coverage vote; the parent study classes the graph layer as a structural guard, never a replacement. Runtime map: an additive frontier-exhaustion guard in convergence.cjs that can only veto STOP while frontier nodes stay open.

Coverage-driven traversal is already described by the typed knowledge graph: the adapter route reason 'remaining question lacks coverage' (reference/03) and omitted edges lower coverage without changing the inline ratio (parent study). Runtime map: uncovered QUESTION nodes in the coverage graph become traversal candidates, which closes iteration 3's gap that the graph discovers but does not steer.

Swarm fan-out is a flat-pool frontier of detached filesystem lineages with a deterministic content-first, ID-tiebreak join that keeps CONTRADICTS variants; wave/depends_on scheduling is rejected and must not be approximated (reference/05, parent study). The decision guide requires distinct fan-out inputs. Runtime map: expansive fan-out must partition frontier nodes across flat-pool lineages instead of giving every lineage the same topic (iteration 3 F8), without reviving wave_orchestration.

Fan-in needs an input-count guard (never synthesize on a partial set and call it complete) and layered fan-in for large branch counts (batch summaries, then the final answer). Runtime map: synthesis checks every frontier node is accounted for; a 100-commit target summarizes per batch before final synthesis.

Separate readiness from execution width: a barrier is valid only when a consumer needs the complete set, cross-set dedupe or total comparison; otherwise stream ready items (S1). Runtime map: frontier nodes are worked as they become ready; only synthesis is a barrier.

Applicability gate: graphs lose on simple lookups and fan-out alone does not justify graph structure; the deciding question is whether width pairs with verification and routing (reference/02). Runtime map: the sub-mode stays opt-in and fits targets that decompose into many independent units (commits, skills/commands), not single-question research.

Ready-made expansion telemetry: fan-out width, branch prune ratio, retry/revisit rate, straggler tax and cost per certified outcome (S1). Runtime map: dashboard metrics for frontier size, pruned nodes and revisits.

Every graph-engineering principle is DESIGN-level and the 036 plane is dark; the typed graph compiler/admission, belief projection and policy compiler are Missing (S6 P4). Runtime map: adopt the principles as additive deep-loop runtime rules (inbox, registry, convergence guard); do not depend on 036 target-state components.

Confirmed: the research append gateway drops graphEvents and most record fields from the state-log projection. The legacy upcast of a research iteration keeps only status, rawNewInfoRatio, ruledOut as digest refs, focus and answeredQuestions; the state-log rows for iterations 1-3 carry no graphEvents, keyQuestions, sourcesQueried or toolsUsed, and ruledOut appears only as legacy-jsonl:<hash>:ruled-out:N. graphEvents still reach the coverage graph through the delta file (iteration 3 F6).

Asymmetry: deep-review iteration records travel whole through the gateway (data: { record: rawEvent }), while research records pass through the lossy legacy upcast. An expansive sub-mode that needs frontier fields on the research state log needs a research iteration stem that preserves them, or must read them from deltas.

Refines iteration 1 F6: the focusAlignment guard evaluates only records that carry both answeredQuestions and keyQuestions and returns notEvaluated when none do; stopDecisionResearchFacts projects keyQuestions only when present. Because the research projection drops keyQuestions, the guard is probably notEvaluated on research runs today rather than penalizing widening (inference: depends on evidenceRecords being state-log rows, not traced).
Expansion is proposal-only: the leaf proposes frontier nodes; only the workflow/reducer admits them under depth and budget bounds.
